Weight Loss Injections

Mounjaro, Wegovy, Ozempic, semaglutide, tirzepatide: there's a lot of buzz, and a lot of confusion. At Facelit, our doctors explain your options in plain language, check whether they're safe for you, and prescribe and monitor the right weekly injection as part of a full weight plan. Less hunger, steady weight loss and real medical care, with no shortcuts.

WeeklyInjection

Overview

What Are Weight Loss Injections?

Weight loss injections are prescription medicines that copy hormones your gut naturally releases after eating, mainly GLP-1 and, with tirzepatide, GIP. These hormones tell your brain you're full, slow down digestion and help control blood sugar. The result: smaller portions feel satisfying, cravings quieten and weight comes off steadily.

The best-known medicines are tirzepatide (Mounjaro) and semaglutide (Wegovy, and Ozempic for diabetes), both injected once a week with a small pen. They're not a magic shot. They work best, and most safely, as part of a doctor-led plan with the right food, activity and support, which is exactly how we use them at Facelit.

Read more: why everyone's talking about them

Before these medicines, prescription weight loss drugs usually gave modest results. In large trials, semaglutide and tirzepatide helped people lose around 15 to 21% of their body weight on average, close to what was once only possible with surgery. They also improve blood sugar, blood pressure and other health markers.

That success has also brought fake pens, online sellers and unsupervised use. Getting them from a doctor who checks your health and monitors you is essential.

How they work

What Happens in Your Body

Three effects working together, so you naturally eat less without fighting hunger all day.

1

Brain: less hunger

Acts on the appetite centre, so you feel satisfied sooner and food "noise" and cravings get quieter.

2

Stomach: fuller for longer

Slows how quickly your stomach empties, so a normal meal keeps you full for hours.

3

Blood sugar: steadier

Helps your body release insulin when sugar rises, reducing spikes, crashes and fat storage.

Compare medicines

Tirzepatide vs Semaglutide vs Liraglutide

The three main weight loss injections, side by side. Tap a medicine to learn more.

Average weight loss in major trialsTap a medicine

Averages from large clinical trials over 56 to 72 weeks, alongside diet and activity. Your results may differ.

Tirzepatide (Mounjaro)

Tirzepatide works on two gut hormones, GLP-1 and GIP, so it has a strong effect on appetite and blood sugar. It has given the largest average weight loss of the three in trials. The dose is built up slowly every 4 weeks.

TypeGLP-1 + GIP (dual action)
InjectionOnce a week

Average weight loss: about 21% on the highest dose over 72 weeks (SURMOUNT-1 trial).

Semaglutide (Wegovy, Ozempic*)

Semaglutide copies the GLP-1 hormone that tells your brain you're full. Wegovy is the higher-dose version made for weight loss. Ozempic is the same medicine at diabetes doses. Several brands and generic versions are now available in India.

TypeGLP-1
InjectionOnce a week

Average weight loss: about 15% over 68 weeks (STEP-1 trial).

Liraglutide (Saxenda and others)

The older daily GLP-1 medicine. It's useful when weekly options aren't suitable, but needs a daily injection and gives less weight loss on average.

TypeGLP-1
InjectionOnce a day

Average weight loss: about 8% over 56 weeks (SCALE trial).

*Ozempic is approved for type 2 diabetes. Brand availability in India changes, so your doctor will advise on the right, genuine product for you.

Your journey

Starting Low, Going Slow

Doses are increased step by step to keep side effects mild. Tap each stage.

A full medical assessment: history, medicines, blood tests (sugar, thyroid, liver, kidney, lipids) and a body composition analysis.

  • Check you're a safe candidate
  • Set realistic targets
  • Plan your food and activity

You start on the lowest dose. This dose is mainly for your body to get used to the medicine, not for big weight loss.

  • We teach you how to inject
  • Mild nausea is common and usually settles
  • Focus on protein and smaller meals

The dose is raised every 4 weeks, if you're coping well, until you reach the dose that works for you.

  • Appetite drops and weight loss picks up
  • Reviews to check side effects and progress
  • Body composition tracking to protect muscle

You stay on your best dose while weight comes down, with regular reviews and repeat blood tests.

  • Steady loss over months
  • Health markers improve
  • Habits built for life after the injections

When you reach your goal, we plan carefully. Many people need to continue at some dose. Others taper slowly with strong lifestyle support.

  • No sudden stopping
  • Nutrition and coaching to hold your results
  • Regular check-ins after stopping

What's included

Our Injection Programme Covers

Doctor assessment and prescription
A full check of your health and medicines, and an honest talk about which option suits you, if any.
Blood tests and body composition
Baseline and follow-up tests so we can track your health and protect your muscle.
Injection training
We show you how to use the pen, where to inject and how to store it.
Regular reviews
Dose changes, side effect support and progress checks at every step.
Nutrition and lifestyle support
Protein-focused eating, activity and coaching, so results last after the injections.

Side effects

Common Side Effects, and How to Manage Them

Most are mild and ease within a few weeks, especially with a slow dose increase. Tap for tips.

Nausea
Eat smaller meals, stop when you're just full, avoid greasy and spicy food, and sip water through the day. It usually improves after each dose increase settles.
Vomiting or diarrhoea
Keep hydrated with water and ORS. Tell us if it lasts more than a day or two. We may slow your dose increase.
Constipation
Drink more water, add fibre gradually, like vegetables, fruit and oats, and keep active.
Acidity and reflux
Avoid large late meals, lying down after eating, and spicy or fried food.
Tiredness or dizziness
Often from eating too little. Make sure you still eat enough protein and drink enough water.
Hair shedding
Can happen with fast weight loss. Enough protein, iron and vitamins helps, and our hair team can support you.

Call us straight away if you have

Warning Signs

  • Severe tummy pain that spreads to your back (possible pancreatitis)
  • Pain in the upper right tummy, fever or yellow eyes (possible gallbladder problem)
  • Vomiting that won't stop, or signs of dehydration
  • A lump or swelling in the neck, or trouble swallowing
  • Signs of an allergic reaction, like a rash, swelling or difficulty breathing

These are rare, but they're why weight loss injections should always be medically supervised.

Myths vs facts

Weight Loss Injection Myths, Busted

"It's a magic shot. I don't need to change anything."
The medicine makes eating less easier, but food choices, protein and activity decide how much fat you lose and how much muscle you keep.
"Once I stop, I'll stay at my new weight."
Many people regain weight after stopping suddenly. A planned taper and lasting habits are key.
"They're only for diabetics."
Some versions are approved specifically for weight management in people without diabetes.
"Buying online is the same."
Fake and unregulated pens are common and can be dangerous. Always get them through a doctor.
"More dose means faster results."
Increasing too fast causes bad side effects. Slow and steady works best.

Who it's for

Who May Benefit

  • Adults with obesity who haven't succeeded with lifestyle changes alone
  • Overweight adults with diabetes, high BP, fatty liver, PCOS or sleep apnoea
  • People with high visceral (belly) fat
  • Anyone ready to combine medicine with better eating and activity

Not for

  • Pregnancy, breastfeeding or planned pregnancy
  • History of medullary thyroid cancer or MEN2
  • Past pancreatitis
  • People who only want to lose a few kilos for an event
  • Under 18 (except under specialist care)

Results

What Results Look Like Over Time

Every body responds differently, but this is a typical pattern.

  1. Weeks 1–4

    Less hunger

    Appetite and cravings drop. Weight loss is gentle while your body adjusts.

  2. Months 2–3

    Steady loss

    Weight comes off more noticeably as the dose increases.

  3. Months 4–6

    Health gains

    Blood sugar, BP and liver numbers often improve on repeat tests.

  4. Months 6–18

    Biggest change

    Most of the weight loss in trials happened over this period.

Why Choose Facelit for Weight Loss Injections?

  1. 01

    Doctor-prescribed and monitored

    Every prescription follows a full medical assessment, and you're reviewed at every dose step.

  2. 02

    We only use approved medicines from authorised sources, never grey-market pens.

  3. 03

Safety first

Who Should Not Take Weight Loss Injections

These medicines are safe for most suitable adults under medical care, but not for everyone.

Not suitable if you

  • Are pregnant, breastfeeding or trying to conceive
  • Have a personal or family history of medullary thyroid cancer or MEN2
  • Have had pancreatitis
  • Are allergic to the medicine

Needs careful assessment if you

  • Have gallbladder disease or severe stomach problems
  • Have kidney disease or diabetic eye disease
  • Take insulin or sulfonylureas (risk of low sugar)
  • Have a history of eating disorders
  • Take oral contraceptive pills (with tirzepatide)

Questions

Weight Loss Injection FAQs

What are weight loss injections?
Weight loss injections are prescription medicines, such as tirzepatide (Mounjaro) and semaglutide (Wegovy), that copy natural gut hormones. They reduce appetite, help you feel full sooner and improve blood sugar, so you eat less without constant hunger. They're used alongside a healthy diet and activity.
How do they work?
They act on the brain's appetite centre to reduce hunger and cravings, slow down how quickly your stomach empties so you stay full longer, and help your body release insulin when blood sugar rises.
How much weight can I lose?
In large trials, people lost on average about 15% of their body weight with semaglutide and about 21% with the highest dose of tirzepatide over roughly 16 to 18 months, alongside diet and activity. Results vary from person to person.
Mounjaro vs Wegovy: which is better?
Tirzepatide (Mounjaro) acts on two hormones and gave more weight loss on average in trials. Semaglutide (Wegovy) is very effective too and has a longer track record. Your doctor will recommend one based on your health, goals, side effects and cost.
Is Ozempic the same as Wegovy?
Both contain semaglutide. Ozempic is approved for type 2 diabetes at lower doses, and Wegovy is the higher-dose version approved for weight management.
Who can take weight loss injections?
They're generally for adults with obesity, or adults who are overweight with weight-related health problems like diabetes, high blood pressure or fatty liver. Because Indians develop these problems at lower weights, your doctor may consider them at a lower BMI than Western guidelines. A full medical assessment is essential.
Who should not take them?
They're not suitable during pregnancy or breastfeeding, or for people with a personal or family history of medullary thyroid cancer or MEN2, or a history of pancreatitis. People with certain gut, kidney or eye problems need careful assessment.
What are the side effects?
Nausea is the most common, especially when the dose goes up. Others include vomiting, diarrhoea, constipation, reflux and tiredness. Most ease within a few weeks. Rare but serious effects include pancreatitis and gallbladder problems, which is why medical supervision matters.
Is the injection painful?
No. It's a tiny needle in a pre-filled pen, injected under the skin of the tummy, thigh or upper arm. Most people barely feel it. We'll teach you how to do it.
How long do I need to take them?
Usually at least several months, and often a year or more, depending on your progress and health. Your doctor will plan how long and how to come off them safely.
Will I regain weight when I stop?
Many people regain some weight if they stop suddenly without changing their habits. That's why we combine injections with nutrition and lifestyle coaching, and plan a gradual, supported taper.
Will I lose muscle?
Fast weight loss can include muscle. Eating enough protein, doing strength exercise and tracking body composition helps protect it, and all of these are part of our programme.
Can I buy weight loss injections online?
Please don't. These are prescription medicines that need medical checks and monitoring. Fake and unregulated products are sold online and can be dangerous.
What if I'm planning a pregnancy?
Tell your doctor. These medicines should be stopped well before trying to conceive (for semaglutide, at least 2 months). Tirzepatide can also make oral contraceptive pills less effective, so extra contraception may be needed.
Where can I get weight loss injections in Kerala?
Facelit offers doctor-supervised weight loss injections as part of our medical weight management programme at our clinics in Trivandrum, Karunagappally (Kollam) and Guruvayur (Thrissur).
How much do weight loss injections cost?
It depends on the medicine, the dose and how long you need it. Book a consultation and your doctor will explain the options and costs clearly.
